# Agent N's Hermes News — Executive Summary

Coverage date: 2026-09-23 · Published: 2026-09-24

Executive Summary

The week belongs to Hermes Desktop's Bot Screen launch: agents' sessions now stream live on your desktop, and you can interactively take over the agent's machine via live desktop passthrough. Official announcements from @NousResearch and @Teknium (the companion post hit 173k views and 1.1k+ likes) were followed by rapid distribution of @tonbistudio's walkthrough — with community reactions like "Finallllly!" confirming this was the most long-awaited feature in recent memory.

On the research side, coverage centered on the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: how Hermes drives the unmodified official Claude Code CLI, and how its keyless authentication keeps credentials entirely with the official CLI via one-time login. Meanwhile, Hermes Agent v0.21.4 adds machine-readable JSONL output for scripters, @rlaope shipped a wave of OMH and Jev tooling, and the broader agent-runtime ecosystem (with AgentProto v0.20.0 and Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0) is increasingly treating Hermes as a first-class integration target.

Releases

  • Hermes Desktop — Bot Screen + Live Desktop Passthrough (headline launch): watch agent sessions stream in real time and interactively take over the agent's machine. Announced by @NousResearch, with @Teknium launching live desktop passthrough in the companion post (173k views, 1.1k+ likes).
  • Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (released 21 September 2026): adds a --format stream-json flag emitting structured JSONL. An immediate upgrade win for anyone scripting against the CLI — the project's steady cadence continues with a focus on automation-friendly, machine-readable output.
  • AgentProto v0.20.0 (22 September 2026): a new open-source TypeScript agent runtime that already lists Hermes among its integrated agents. Worth tracking for interoperability with your Hermes setups.
  • Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: hardens MCP security with per-invocation session scoping — a pattern directly relevant to Hermes's own MCP discovery and integration configuration.

Community

  • Bot Screen launch reception: Official onboarding moved fast — @NousResearch distributed @tonbistudio's walkthrough (44k views) and @Teknium amplified the guide video. Reactions like "Finallllly!" signal strong demand finally met.
  • Builder ecosystem momentum: @rlaope shipped oh-my-hermes (OMH) support for Jev-Skills, Model Routing, aliases, and plugins, plus the open-source jeval tool for Jev evaluation and visualization — a material expansion of the community plugin ecosystem and better tooling for evaluating Jev model outputs.
  • Core-team support stayed hands-on: @Teknium rebutted a plugin cache-bug claim by demanding a reproducible issue path, confirmed a quick community-reported fix, and clarified the new tooling is Nous-built rather than Anthropic's. @NousResearch advised a user on accessing Hermes via iMessage with any model.
  • Sentiment watch: a widely shared take that Claude Opus 5.5 (GA'd the day before coverage) is impressive but Claude Code lags — read as quiet confidence in Hermes Agent as the driver layer.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Getting started with Bot Screen: follow @tonbistudio's walkthrough (distributed via @NousResearch and amplified by @Teknium) for the fastest path from install to watching — and taking over — live agent sessions.
  • Running Hermes on top of Claude: two deep-dives on the Hermes-Claude plugin cover the pipeline architecture that lets Hermes drive the unmodified official Claude Code CLI, plus a security-focused guide to its keyless authentication flow — credentials stay entirely with the official CLI via one-time login. Directly actionable if you're running or evaluating the plugin.
  • Scripting against the CLI: upgrade to Hermes Agent v0.21.4 and use --format stream-json to consume structured JSONL events instead of parsing free-form terminal output.
  • Quick access tip: per @NousResearch, you can reach Hermes via iMessage with any model — no extra setup required for casual use.
